patients.summary: Retired postal worker with COPD GOLD II, hypertension and hyperlipidemia who joined the practice a month after a September 2024 MI with an LAD stent. Over the next year he had pneumococcal meningitis, an ICU stay for hypoxemic respiratory failure and an ICU stay for pneumonia with septic shock complicated by arterial cannulation during central line placement; he has recovered and is followed for his chronic conditions.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

67 yo retired letter carrier transferring care; his prior office is closing. Came with his wife and a bag of bottles and inhalers, which we went through together.

The big event: heart attack about a month ago (admitted ~9/9 at the county medical center). Cath, one drug-eluting stent to the LAD on 9/10. Home after a few days. No chest pain since. Walking the driveway and to the mailbox daily, a little more each week. Has his first cardiology follow-up in early November.

Lungs: told he has COPD, "stage 2," for a number of years. On tiotropium HandiHaler daily plus fluticasone/salmeterol twice daily, albuterol maybe twice a week. Gets winded on a flight of stairs, baseline for him. No recent flares he can name.

Also long-standing high blood pressure and high cholesterol, both treated.

SMOKING: 35 pack-years. Quit the day he went into the hospital in September and has not had one since. "The scare did it." Not using patches or gum. Discussed relapse risk; he declines any aid for now, will call if cravings get hard.
Alcohol: a beer or two on the weekend.
Retired from the post office. Lives in Sunderland with his wife.

FAMILY: father died of an MI, age 62. Mother living, has COPD. Older brother with type 2 diabetes.

ALLERGIES: none to medications.

CURRENT MEDS (reconciled from bottles):
- aspirin 81 mg daily
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily
- metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily
- lisinopril 10 mg daily
- tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
- fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50, 1 inhalation BID
- albuterol HFA 90 mcg, 1-2 puffs q4-6h PRN wheeze/SOB

ROS: no chest pain, no orthopnea, no leg swelling, no syncope. Chronic mild exertional dyspnea as above. No cough change, no fever.

EXAM: Vitals as charted. Pleasant, in no distress, speaking full sentences. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no JVD. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs: mildly diminished breath sounds throughout, no wheeze, no crackles. Right radial access site healed. Abdomen soft. Extremities warm, no edema.

ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. CAD s/p MI with LAD stent (9/2024): stable. Continue aspirin, atorvastatin, metoprolol, lisinopril. Keep the cardiology appointment.
2. COPD, GOLD II: stable on current inhalers. Technique checked on the HandiHaler, good. 
3. HTN: at goal today.
4. Hyperlipidemia: fasting lipids today.
5. Tobacco dependence, in early remission: congratulated. Eligible for lung cancer screening; will set up after he's further from the MI, he'd rather not have one more appointment this fall.
6. Health maintenance: flu (high dose) and COVID boosters given. Hep C screen today. Reports colonoscopy around 2019 was fine and a tetanus shot about then; will confirm in records.

Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, HCV Ab.
Records release signed for prior office and the hospital. Return in about 2-3 months, sooner after cardiology if they change anything.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Mr. Wojcik,

Your blood work from Tuesday looks good. Kidney function, liver tests, blood counts and sugar (A1c) are all in the normal range. Your LDL ("bad") cholesterol is under 70, which is where we want it after a heart attack, so the atorvastatin is doing its job. Hepatitis C screen was negative.

No changes. Talk soon.

COUNTY MEDICAL CENTER — CARDIOLOGY INPATIENT SERVICE
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit: 09/09/2024   Discharge: 09/12/2024

DIAGNOSIS: Acute myocardial infarction. Coronary artery disease.
PROCEDURES: 09/10/2024 diagnostic left heart catheterization via right radial artery; percutaneous coronary intervention with placement of one drug-eluting stent to the left anterior descending artery.

HOSPITAL COURSE: 67-year-old man with COPD, hypertension and hyperlipidemia, active smoker, presented through the ED and was diagnosed with acute MI. Taken for catheterization the following morning; culprit LAD lesion treated with a single drug-eluting stent without complication. Course otherwise uneventful. Ambulating without symptoms prior to discharge. Strongly counseled on smoking cessation; patient states he has quit.

ALLERGIES: NKDA

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
aspirin 81 mg daily
atorvastatin 40 mg daily
metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily
lisinopril 10 mg daily
tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 one inhalation twice daily
albuterol 90 mcg inhaler every 4-6 hours as needed

FOLLOW-UP: Outpatient cardiology in 6-8 weeks. Primary care within 1 month.

Scanned and reviewed, PCP.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group — office letter
Date of visit: 11/06/2024

Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Wojcik today, about eight weeks out from his myocardial infarction and LAD drug-eluting stent (9/10/2024). He is doing well. No angina, no rest symptoms, no palpitations or presyncope. His breathing is at his COPD baseline. He has not smoked since admission and is walking daily.

Exam: BP and heart rate well controlled on his regimen. Regular rhythm, no murmur or gallop, lungs with mildly reduced air movement and no crackles, no edema. Right radial site healed.

Allergies: NKDA.
Medications: aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol PRN.

Impression: CAD s/p recent MI and LAD stent, clinically stable.
Plan: continue current medications without change. Continue walking program. Return in 9 months, or sooner with symptoms.

Thank you for allowing me to share in his care.

— Cardiology

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
COUNTY MEDICAL CENTER — EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Visit: 12/11/2024 14:20

CC: headache, fever, confusion

HPI: 67M brought in by his wife. Two days of severe headache and high fevers, increasingly confused. Wife says he has been slower to answer her and keeps saying his neck hurts and is stiff. History obtained mostly from wife given his mental status.

PMH: COPD (GOLD II), CAD with MI and LAD DES 9/2024, HTN, HLD.
Meds: ASA 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 10, tiotropium, fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: ex-smoker (35 pk-yr, quit 9/2024), occasional beer, retired postal worker.

VS on arrival: T 39.2 C (102.5 F), HR 110, BP 130/85.

EXAM: Ill-appearing. Oriented to person only — not to time or place. Neck: flexion meets resistance and is painful. Lungs: breath sounds decreased at the right base, otherwise clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. No rash. Moves all extremities.

LABS: WBC 15.0 K/uL. Glucose 150 mg/dL.
LP performed at 16:00. CSF cloudy. CSF WBC 2,000/uL, protein 180 mg/dL, glucose 30 mg/dL. Gram stain: gram-positive cocci in pairs.

MDM: CSF picture and Gram stain are consistent with bacterial meningitis, pneumococcal. Empiric ceftriaxone, vancomycin and dexamethasone started in the ED, dexamethasone given with the first antibiotic dose.

DISPOSITION: admitted to the medicine service.
Dx: bacterial meningitis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae.

Received by fax 12/13; reviewed by PCP.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary — Medicine
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
COUNTY MEDICAL CENTER — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 12/11/2024 from the ED. Discharged 12/21/2024.

PRINCIPAL DIAGNOSIS: Bacterial meningitis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae.
Other active problems: COPD GOLD II; CAD s/p MI and LAD DES 9/2024; hypertension; hyperlipidemia.

COURSE: Presented with two days of headache, fever and confusion; CSF consistent with bacterial meningitis with gram-positive diplococci on Gram stain. Treated with IV ceftriaxone and vancomycin plus dexamethasone. CSF culture grew Streptococcus pneumoniae on 12/13; vancomycin and dexamethasone were stopped at that point and ceftriaxone continued. Fevers settled by hospital day 3, and his mental status returned to baseline around the same time; wife agrees he is himself. He completed 10 days of IV ceftriaxone in hospital. Breathing remained at his baseline on home inhalers throughout. Cardiac medications continued. Ambulating independently at discharge, no focal neurologic findings.

ALLERGIES: NKDA

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS (unchanged from home):
aspirin 81 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily; lisinopril 10 mg daily; tiotropium 18 mcg daily; fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID; albuterol PRN.
No antibiotics at discharge.

FOLLOW-UP: PCP within 1-2 weeks.

Scanned to chart; PCP reviewed. TCM call made 12/23 by RN — home, eating, no headache, appointment 12/30 confirmed.

documents.title: Call From Patient's Wife
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called to let us know Chad was admitted overnight at the county medical center with meningitis. She was at his side the whole time and wanted to know whether she needs antibiotics herself. Explained that the hospital has identified the bacteria as the pneumococcal type, which is not one where household contacts are routinely given preventive antibiotics, but to check with the inpatient team since they have the final culture. She's feeling well. Asked her to call us when he has a discharge date so we can see him soon after. Message to PCP.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here 9 days after discharge for pneumococcal meningitis (admitted 12/11, 10 days IV ceftriaxone). Wife with him. Tired, napping in the afternoons, appetite coming back. No headache since about day 4 in the hospital. Neck feels normal. No fevers at home. Hearing and vision feel the same as before to him. Breathing at his usual. Down a few pounds. Taking all meds as before, nothing new added at discharge.

O: Vitals as charted, afebrile. Alert, oriented x3, conversational, tells the story of the admission accurately (with a few gaps from the first days). Neck supple, full flexion without pain. Lungs: diminished but symmetric, no focal findings at the right base today. Heart regular. Gait steady. Cranial nerves grossly intact.

A/P:
1. Pneumococcal meningitis — treated, clinically resolved. Labs to make sure counts and kidneys are back to normal after the IV course. Gave return precautions for any recurrent headache/fever/confusion.
2. Pneumococcal vaccine: he is a good candidate now; will give the conjugate vaccine at the wellness visit in February when he's further out from the illness.
3. Lung cancer screening: LDCT ordered for January now that the cardiac and infectious issues have quieted down.
4. CAD, HTN, COPD: stable, no changes.

RTC February for Medicare wellness visit.

documents.title: Labs After the Hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Chad, the blood work from yesterday is reassuring: white count is back to normal, and kidney function and electrolytes are fine after all the IV medicine. Rest up and happy new year.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (baseline)
Indication: 67-year-old former smoker, 35 pack-years, quit 2024.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without IV contrast.
Comparison: None available.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Airways patent. Heart size normal; coronary stent noted in the LAD territory. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable. No suspicious osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months.

documents.title: CT Scan Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Chad — your screening CT scan of the lungs showed no nodules or spots of concern. The radiologist calls it Lung-RADS 1, the best category. We'll repeat it once a year. See you in February.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
INITIAL AWV

Feeling back to himself after the December meningitis admission; energy close to normal now, regained some weight. Walking most days when the roads aren't icy. Still no cigarettes, five months now. No chest pain, breathing at baseline, albuterol a couple of times a week.

Functional: independent in all ADLs/IADLs, drives, manages his own pills with a weekly box. No falls. Hearing — no change noticed by him or his wife. Vision: readers only.
Mood: PHQ-2 = 0.
Cognition: alert, three-word recall 3/3, clock normal.
Home safety reviewed. Advance directive: wife is his health care proxy; he'll bring the form in.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs diminished bilaterally, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.

Prevention:
- PCV20 today (pneumococcal meningitis 12/2024, COPD).
- Shingrix #1 today; #2 in 2-6 months, nurse visit.
- Flu and COVID done in October.
- Tdap 2019 on file.
- Colonoscopy 2019 normal, next 2029.
- LDCT 1/2025 Lung-RADS 1, annual.
- AAA screening: ultrasound ordered.
- Hep C neg 10/2024.

Chronic problems: CAD s/p LAD stent, COPD, HTN, hyperlipidemia — stable, labs from October and December reviewed, no changes.

Personalized plan given. Follow-up in ~3 months.

reports.text:
ULTRASOUND, ABDOMINAL AORTA (AAA SCREENING)
Indication: Male, 67, former smoker.
Findings: The abdominal aorta is visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation. Maximal anteroposterior diameter 2.0 cm in the infrarenal segment. No aneurysmal dilation. Common iliac arteries normal in caliber where seen.
reports.conclusion: Normal caliber abdominal aorta. No abdominal aortic aneurysm.

documents.author: critical care

COUNTY MEDICAL CENTER — MEDICAL ICU
Note date: 04/08/2025 08:10

67-year-old man, COPD GOLD II, CAD with MI and LAD stent in 9/2024, pneumococcal meningitis treated 12/2024. Intubated 04/03 for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure; ventilator day 5.

Current support: pressure support 5 cm H2O, PEEP 5 cm H2O.
VS: T 37.2 C, BP 135/85, HR 88, RR 16, SpO2 94% on these settings.
ABG (drawn ~30 min prior, same settings, FiO2 40%): pH 7.32 / PaCO2 45 / PaO2 78.

Exam: awake and alert off sedation, follows commands consistently, sustains a head lift off the pillow for 5 seconds. Strong cough with suctioning. Breath sounds diminished bilaterally, no wheeze.

Assessment: tolerating minimal support with good mental status, airway protection and cough. Meets our criteria for extubation.
Plan: extubate this morning to nasal cannula; incentive spirometry, early mobility; resume home inhalers.

Addendum 11:40: extubated without difficulty at 09:15. Comfortable on 2 L, speaking full sentences.

Received with discharge packet 4/14.

documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
COUNTY MEDICAL CENTER — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 04/03/2025 — Discharge 04/12/2025

DIAGNOSIS: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure without hypercapnic encephalopathy.
COMORBIDITIES: COPD GOLD II; CAD, MI with LAD drug-eluting stent 9/2024; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; pneumococcal meningitis 12/2024, treated.

COURSE: Admitted early on 04/03 in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure and intubated in the ED; transferred to the ICU. Mechanically ventilated for five days. On 04/08 tolerated pressure support 5/5 with an acceptable gas and good mental status and cough, and was extubated the same morning. Weaned to room air over the next two days. Transferred to the floor, worked with PT, ambulating the hallway independently before discharge. No reintubation.

ALLERGIES: NKDA

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS: no changes from home — aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID, albuterol 90 mcg q4-6h PRN.

FOLLOW-UP: PCP in 1-2 weeks. Outpatient pulmonology recommended.

Reviewed by PCP 4/14. RN TCM call 4/14: home, breathing OK, appointment 4/22.

documents.title: Post-ICU Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Ten days out from a 4/3-4/12 ICU admission for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, intubated five days, extubated 4/8. Discharge summary and ICU notes reviewed.

He says the week is mostly a blank. Since home: sore throat from the tube is gone, voice back to normal. Short of breath on the stairs, about where he was before. Using albuterol once or twice a day this week, tapering off. No fevers, no chest pain. Sleeping in his own bed, flat. Lost about 4 lb in hospital.
Inhalers — showed me his technique for both, good. Still not smoking.

Exam: vitals as charted, room air sat acceptable at rest and after a lap of the hallway. Alert, a little deconditioned. Lungs with diminished breath sounds both sides, no wheeze or crackles. Heart regular. No edema. Calves soft.

A/P
- Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, resolved; recovering at home.
- COPD GOLD II: no changes to tiotropium or fluticasone/salmeterol. Referral to pulmonology — he has not had a lung doctor since his old office, and after an ICU stay he should.
- CAD/HTN: stable, same meds.
- CBC, BMP today.
- Shingrix #2 due — nurse visit next month.
Call right away for worsening breathing. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Labs From Your Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood counts and chemistry panel from yesterday are normal. Nothing to change. The pulmonology office should call you to schedule; let us know if you haven't heard in a week.

documents.title: Nurse Visit — Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for 2nd Shingrix. Feeling well, afebrile. Had a tired, achy day after the first dose in Feb, nothing else. Dose given left deltoid, lot recorded. Tolerated without issue. Series now complete. Reminded about pulmonology appointment 6/11.

documents.title: Referral Status
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pulmonology office confirms receipt of referral and records; pt scheduled 6/11 at 10:30. Pt aware, told to bring all inhalers and to hold albuterol the morning of the visit if he can, per their breathing-test instructions.

reports.text: Spirometry with bronchodilator. Acceptable and repeatable efforts. Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.62. Post-bronchodilator FEV1 61% of predicted.
reports.conclusion: Obstructive ventilatory defect consistent with COPD, GOLD 2 (moderate) by post-bronchodilator FEV1.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group — consultation
Date of service: 06/11/2025
Referring: PCP

Reason: COPD, recent ICU admission (4/2025) for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure.

History: 68-year-old former smoker (35 pack-years, stopped 9/2024 after an MI). Known COPD for years on tiotropium and fluticasone/salmeterol with albuterol as needed. ICU admission in April with intubation for five days, extubated without event. Also hospitalized for pneumococcal meningitis in December 2024. Since April he is back at his baseline: dyspnea after a flight of stairs or a brisk walk uphill, none at rest. Albuterol a few times a week. No regular sputum.

Meds: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 10, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID, albuterol PRN. NKDA.

Exam: comfortable at rest, room air saturation normal. Mildly prolonged expiration, diminished breath sounds, no wheeze or crackles. No clubbing. No edema.

Spirometry today: post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.62; FEV1 61% predicted.

Impression: COPD, GOLD 2, confirmed by spirometry. Currently stable on his maintenance regimen.

Recommendations:
1. Continue tiotropium and fluticasone/salmeterol as prescribed; albuterol as needed.
2. Stay up to date with vaccines — he has had PCV20 this year; flu and COVID each fall; RSV vaccine is reasonable this fall.
3. Continue abstinence from tobacco.
4. Follow up here in one year, sooner if needed.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: ICU Procedure Note — Central Venous Catheter
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
COUNTY MEDICAL CENTER — MEDICAL ICU PROCEDURE NOTE
Date: 10/02/2025

Patient: 68M with COPD GOLD II, CAD with MI and LAD stent 9/2024, prior ICU stay 4/2025 for hypoxemic respiratory failure, now in septic shock from pneumonia requiring norepinephrine.
Indication: central venous access for vasopressor and multiple infusions.
Pre-procedure VS: BP 90/60, HR 110, RR 22, SpO2 92% on 2 L NC.
Consent from patient and wife. Time-out performed. Full sterile barrier.

First site, ultrasound guidance: vessel accessed, but the guidewire would not pass and aspirate through the needle was bright red and brisk. Needle held in place and a blood gas sent from that syringe immediately: pH 7.45, PaCO2 35, PaO2 95, HCO3 24 — consistent with arterial puncture. No dilator or catheter was passed. Needle withdrawn and firm pressure held for 10 minutes with hemostasis; no hematoma on repeat ultrasound.
Second site, ultrasound guidance: venous position confirmed before dilation; triple-lumen catheter placed without difficulty, good blood return all ports, position confirmed.

Complication: accidental arterial cannulation (needle only), recognized and managed as above, without apparent harm.
Patient tolerated the procedure. Vasopressor moved to the central line.

Received 10/14 with discharge records.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary — Critical Care
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
COUNTY MEDICAL CENTER — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission 10/01/2025 — Discharge 10/11/2025

PRINCIPAL DIAGNOSIS: Septic shock due to pneumonia.
SECONDARY: Accidental arterial cannulation during central venous catheter placement (10/02), no sequelae. COPD GOLD II. CAD, MI with LAD drug-eluting stent 9/2024. Hypertension. Hyperlipidemia. Prior: acute hypoxemic respiratory failure 4/2025, resolved; pneumococcal meningitis 12/2024, treated.

COURSE: Presented the evening of 10/01 with pneumonia and hypotension and was admitted to the ICU. Sputum sent for culture on admission; grew normal respiratory flora without a predominant pathogen. Treated with broad IV antibiotics. Required norepinephrine; central venous access on 10/02 was complicated by arterial puncture at the first site, recognized before dilation and held without hematoma, with the line placed at a second site. Vasopressor weaned off over the following 48 hours. Did not require intubation; oxygen weaned to room air before transfer to the floor. Antibiotic course completed in hospital. Central line removed before discharge, site clean. Walking independently with PT at discharge.

ALLERGIES: NKDA

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS: unchanged home regimen — aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID, albuterol PRN. No antibiotics at discharge.

FOLLOW-UP: PCP 1-2 weeks; repeat chest imaging in 6-8 weeks.

Reviewed by PCP 10/14.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Third hospitalization in under a year. 10/1-10/11, ICU: septic shock from pneumonia, on norepinephrine, not intubated this time. Central line placement 10/2 complicated by an arterial puncture at the first site — needle only, held, no hematoma — line went in at a second site. Sputum culture: normal flora. IV antibiotics finished in hospital. Discharge summary and procedure note reviewed.

Today: tired but improving daily. Cough mostly gone, no sputum, no fevers. Dyspnea at his baseline. Both line sites healed; no neck swelling, pain or bruising. Eating well. Meds as before.
He and his wife are frustrated with how the year has gone; he asks whether something is "wrong with his immune system." We talked it through — each illness has had its own cause, and his vaccines are now up to date (PCV20 in Feb, flu/COVID/RSV in Sept). He seemed reassured.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile, room air sat normal. Neck: no hematoma, no bruit, puncture sites healed. Lungs diminished, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. Pneumonia with septic shock — resolved clinically. CXR in ~4 weeks per discharge plan. CBC/BMP today.
2. Arterial cannulation during CVC placement — no sequelae, resolved.
3. COPD, CAD, HTN, HLD — no changes.
4. LDCT due in January; ordered.
Return sooner for fever, worse breathing, or any neck swelling.

reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, ANNUAL LUNG CANCER SCREENING
Indication: 68-year-old former smoker, 35 pack-years, quit 2024.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without IV contrast.
Comparison: 01/21/2025.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation; no residual opacity. No effusion or pneumothorax. Central airways clear. Heart normal in size; LAD stent. No enlarged mediastinal or hilar nodes. Upper abdomen and bones unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Next annual low-dose CT in 12 months.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit (subsequent)
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
SUBSEQUENT AWV, age 68

Quiet four months, which after last year he is glad of. No hospital visits since October. Breathing at his usual; albuterol a couple of times a week, more on the cold mornings. No chest pain. Still smoke-free, about 17 months. Holidays at his brother's went fine.

Function: independent; drives; does the shopping. No falls in the past year. Hearing and vision unchanged.
PHQ-2: 0.
Cognition: no concerns from him or wife; recall 3/3.
Advance directive: health care proxy form (wife) now scanned to chart.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. RRR. No edema. Skin: no concerning lesions on a brief check.

Screening/immunization review:
- LDCT 1/2026 Lung-RADS 1; next 1/2027.
- Colonoscopy 2019 normal; next 2029.
- AAA US 3/2025 normal; done.
- PCV20 2/2025; Shingrix complete 5/2025; RSV 9/2025; Tdap 2019 (due 2029); flu/COVID 9/2025.
- HCV neg.

Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c.
Chronic problems stable on current regimen. Written prevention plan updated. RTC ~3 months.

documents.title: Wellness Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Chad — your wellness labs are all in good shape. Blood counts normal, kidney and liver numbers normal, A1c in the normal (non-diabetic) range, and LDL cholesterol remains below 70. Keep doing what you're doing.

documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group
Follow-up visit 03/17/2026

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Wojcik was seen for his scheduled coronary follow-up, now 18 months after MI and LAD stenting. Since his August visit he was admitted in October with pneumonia and septic shock, which he has recovered from; no cardiac events during that stay were reported to us. He denies angina, rest or exertional chest discomfort, palpitations or syncope. Activity is walking, limited by breath rather than chest symptoms.

Vitals: blood pressure and pulse within goal. Exam: regular rhythm, normal S1/S2, no murmur; lungs diminished; no peripheral edema.

Allergies: none known.
Current medications: aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily; inhaled tiotropium and fluticasone/salmeterol, albuterol as needed.

Impression: stable coronary artery disease, no angina.
Plan: continue present therapy. Return in one year.

Sincerely,
Cardiology

Routine follow-up, moved from April.

Doing well. Spring has been good for his breathing; back to walking the full loop by the river most mornings. Rescue inhaler maybe once a week. No cough, no sputum. No chest pressure on the walks. Home BP checks at the pharmacy machine run in the 120s. Taking everything as prescribed. Pulmonology annual in June, cardiology saw him in March with no changes.

Exam: vitals as charted. Breathing unlabored, lungs diminished without wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.

- COPD GOLD 2: well controlled, same inhalers.
- CAD s/p MI/stent: asymptomatic, continue aspirin, statin, beta blocker, ACE inhibitor.
- HTN: at goal.
- HLD: LDL < 70 in February.
Next visit August with BMP and lipids. Fall vaccines after that.

COPD GOLD 2 (spirometry 6/2025: post-BD FEV1/FVC 0.62, FEV1 61% predicted). Since last year: hospitalized October 2025 for pneumonia with septic shock, recovered fully; follow-up chest x-ray in November was clear and his January screening CT was negative. No COPD exacerbations treated with steroids. Dyspnea on stairs and hills, stable; albuterol about weekly. Off tobacco since 9/2024.

Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID, albuterol PRN; cardiac meds per cardiology. NKDA.

Exam: comfortable, room air saturation normal at rest. Diminished breath sounds, prolonged expiratory phase, no wheeze or crackles. No edema.

Assessment: COPD GOLD 2, stable on LAMA plus ICS/LABA.
Plan: no changes. Fall influenza and COVID vaccines. Return in 12 months.
